rules.text: Never log passwords, tokens, or API keys.
Always mask personal data in log output.
Never log full credit card numbers or bank account details.
Never write session identifiers to log files.
Always include a request ID in error logs for traceability.
Never log request bodies for authentication endpoints.
Passwords must be hashed with bcrypt or argon2 before storage.
Never return password hashes in API responses.
Session tokens must expire after 30 minutes of inactivity.
Login attempts must be rate limited per account and per IP address.
Failed login responses must not reveal whether the username exists.
Password reset tokens must be single use and expire within 15 minutes.
Multi-factor authentication codes must not be reused.
Never store authentication tokens in local storage in browser code.
All user input must be validated before use.
Never build SQL queries with string concatenation.
Uploaded files must be checked for type and size before processing.
Never pass user input to shell commands without escaping.
Never render user-supplied HTML without sanitizing it first.
Redirect targets must be validated against an allow list.
Never commit secrets, keys, or passwords to the repository.
Secrets must be loaded from environment variables or a secret manager.
Never print environment variables that contain secrets.
Development configuration must never point at production databases.
All external traffic must use TLS 1.2 or later.
Personal data must be encrypted at rest.
Database backups must be encrypted and access controlled.
Never disable certificate verification in production code.
Database access must go through the repository layer.
Handlers must never query the database directly.
Business logic must not live in API handlers.
Services must not import from API handler modules.
Shared utilities must not depend on feature modules.
External API calls must go through a client module, never directly from business logic.
Background jobs must be idempotent.
Cross-module communication must use defined service interfaces, not direct access to internal files.
Every endpoint must return a consistent error format with a code and a message.
List endpoints must support pagination.
Breaking changes to public endpoints must be versioned.
Endpoints that change data must validate the request body against a schema.
Response times for read endpoints must stay under 300 milliseconds at the 95th percentile.
Endpoints must return 401 for missing credentials and 403 for insufficient permissions.
Schema changes must be delivered as migration files.
Migrations must be reversible.
Deleting user records must remove or anonymize related personal data.
Timestamps must be stored in UTC.
Money values must be stored as integers in the smallest currency unit.
New features must include tests for the main path and one failure case.
Bug fixes must start with a failing test that reproduces the bug.
Existing tests must pass before a change is merged.
Repository layer code must have integration tests against a real database.
Public API endpoints must have contract tests.
Test data must not contain real personal information.
Forms must show validation errors next to the field that caused them.
Pages must remain usable at 320 pixels width.
User-facing text must be stored in translation files, never hardcoded in components.
Components must not fetch data directly.
Data loading must go through hooks or services.
Pull requests must link to the related ticket.
Reviewers must check the change against the security rules before approval.
Pull requests that change the database schema must include the migration file.
Each pull request must pass the linter before review.
Functions should not exceed 50 lines.
Files should not exceed 400 lines.
Commits should not mix formatting changes with logic changes.
Never force push to the main branch.
Dependencies with known critical vulnerabilities must not be added.
Developers should avoid adding a dependency for a function that the standard library provides.
Queries must use parameters, never string interpolation.
Queries that return many rows must be paginated or streamed.
Long-running queries must have a timeout set.
Every table must have a primary key.
Foreign keys must be defined in the database, not only in application code.
Soft-deleted rows must be excluded from default queries.
Database connections must be released after use.
Connection pool size must be configured per service, not hardcoded.
Database credentials must not appear in source code.
Migrations must be reviewed by a second developer before running in production.
Destructive migrations must be preceded by a backup.
Migrations should not depend on application code.
Resource identifiers in paths should not expose internal database sequence numbers.
Errors should not include stack traces in production responses.
Responses should not include fields the client did not request when a field selection is supported.
The API version must appear in the URL path, such as /v1/users.
Clients exceeding the rate limit must receive status 429 with a retry-after header.
Shared components must live in the common components folder.
Components must not contain business rules.
Server data must be cached and invalidated after mutations.
Interactive elements must be reachable by keyboard.
Images must have alternative text.
Color must not be the only way to convey information.
Modal dialogs must trap focus while open.
Deployments must be performed through the CI pipeline, never by hand.
Every deployment must have a rollback plan documented in the release notes.
Production deployments must not occur on Fridays after 14:00.
Every service must expose a health check endpoint.
Errors must be reported to the central error tracker with the request ID.
Alerts must link to a runbook.
Incidents must be recorded in the incident tracker within one hour of detection.
Post-incident reviews must be written without assigning personal blame.
Hotfixes must be merged back into the main branch the same day.
